bugs.text: startGame never builds a formation or entry groups for stage 1 (enemies=[]), so the first frame of play finds no enemies and declares the stage clear. No enemy ever appears in the game.

'stageclear' mode is never handled: stageClearTimer is never decremented and startStage is only reachable from challengeSummary, so the game soft-locks on 'STAGE 1 CLEAR!' forever; Enter does nothing (only works in title mode).
spawnGroup is only called by the challenge stage; normal-stage enemies would stay 'pending' indefinitely even if the formation were built, which would also block stage clear.
Rescue can never happen: destroyEnemy makes the captive hostile and clears boss.captured before freeCaptured runs, so the dual fighter is unobtainable.
Challenge waves create enemies that are never added to game.enemies; kind 'challenge' falls through to the normal loop path; makeChallengePath unused.
Formation is 10 columns x 5 rows = 50 enemies with 10 bosses, not 4/16/20.
Boss always scores 400+ (even in formation); no diving bonus for Zako/Goei.
Title score table lists Boss Galaga as 200000 PTS.
HUD shows 3 reserve ships while a ship is in play (should be 2).
formation.done is never set true, so the formation never breathes.
sfxEnemyHit is defined but never called.
Boss Galaga is excluded from player body collision.

summary: The file is tidy on the surface: a proper 60 Hz fixed-timestep loop, integer-scaled 224x288 canvas, a twinkling multi-coloured starfield, code-drawn sprites, synthesized audio and a title screen, all loading without console errors. But the gameplay is never wired together: starting a game never builds the formation, so the stage is declared clear on the first frame and the game then sits on 'STAGE 1 CLEAR!' forever because nothing handles the stageclear mode. Even with that fixed, normal-stage entry groups are never spawned, the formation is 50 enemies with 10 bosses, rescue of a captured fighter is logically impossible, and challenge-stage enemies are never added to the world. The play-test screenshots confirm the player alone on an empty field under 'STAGE 1 CLEAR!' for the whole 90 s. Much of a Galaga design exists as dead code, but as delivered it is not a game.
